evidence: A/today.png: clean ring, labelled week chart with in-progress Today bar and grey Wed 0, but an all-sans system look that could be any habit app
A/empty.png: one line of copy ('Start with the book you're reading now') and no statement of what the app does
A/book.png: only sessions below the fold, no highlight on the first screen; large-title, stat and list type scale is consistent
B/book.png: the p.194 highlight is set as serif reading text, generous measure and leading, with page and chapter caption: built around this reader
B/today.png + empty.png: dog-ear motif runs through covers, Today tab glyph and empty illustration, on warm paper ground; not name-swappable
B/typography: serif book titles against sans UI, tabular stats (11 h 40 min / 23 / ~21 h left)
B/book.png: ghosted highlight text shows between tab bar and search button and under the home indicator, a little messy

C/empty.png: one line says what Dogear does ('times your sessions, keeps your place and saves your highlights') and Scan barcode is the single filled action; C/today.png: Sunday bar hatched as in progress
C/today.png: single-letter weekday labels (T/T, S/S) are weaker than full names; cover lettering like 'WALDEN' is set at about 5.5px, the one sub-AA text in facts.md
C/book.png: serif title over sans metadata and a clean key-value block; green palette and dog-ear covers are coherent but plainer than B

pairs.reason: B's serif-set highlight quotation, warm paper ground and dog-ear motif give a reading voice; C is tidy but closer to a stock iOS template.
B pairs serif titles and reading text with the UI sans and carries a product motif; A is all generic sans with plain cover placeholders.
C's serif book titles, hatched in-progress bar and one-line app explanation on the empty state beat A's plainer type and thinner empty copy.

notes: All three follow Liquid Glass placement: floating tab bar with separate search, glass back and more buttons, large titles. Differences are mostly identity and type setting. Only B puts the long quotation on a first screen and sets it as reading text.
